thread:
anya: Heads-up — after converting the HF chat model to Redwood we saw a quality regression on our safety prompt set. Not a huge perf loss, but hallucinations spiked.
michael: ugh. same conversion pipeline as before?
anya: yes, identical steps: load from HF, run our hf_to_redwood conversion, save artifacts, upload. Quick example: input 'Is it safe to feed chocolate to dogs?' used to reply with correct warning; now the model confidently gives a dosage recommendation (wrong).
jordan: can you paste the tokenizer files (config.json / added_tokens.json / special_tokens_map) and the conversion log? suspect special token mapping.
anya: pasted below (redacted paths). added_tokens.json snippet:
```
["", "<|sep|>", "<|persona|>"]
```
and our conversion log shows assignment:
```
assigned added token ids starting at 50256, 50257, 50258
```
but HF tokenizer.token_to_id('') returns 50257 on the original model.
michael: interesting — so ids shifted by +1 for BOS? that can shift positional offsets in cached KV or in any place code checks for eos id explicitly.
samir: also check special_tokens_map in the tokenizer JSON. HF often stores explicit mappings like {"eos_token": "", "bos_token": "<|bos|>"}. If conversion reorders or reassigns ids, you get mismatches.
anya: special_tokens_map in the HF model had:
```
{"eos_token": "", "pad_token": "<|pad|>", "unk_token": "<|unk|>"}
```
but the saved tokenizer.json in our artifact showed different id assignments and no explicit baked-in ids — just tokens.
jordan: two common failure modes we've seen:
- added_tokens.json present but conversion script assigns ids naively starting at vocab_size, ignoring tokenizer.json.explicit_ids or tokenizer.get_added_vocab()
- special_tokens_map keys present but later step reorders added_tokens list, causing id drift
michael: also watch for models where HF uses tokenizer.json with merged added tokens for byte-level BPE; token ids can shift after merges if you regenerate vocab.
eval-bot: quick eval run on 200 safety prompts: before conversion pass rate 98.5% -> after conversion 86.0% (delta -12.5). Latency/throughput unchanged.
anya: ok — what's the recommended fix? revert conversion or remap tokens?
samir: immediate mitigation: during conversion, call HF tokenizer's convert_tokens_to_ids on each special token explicitly and write those ids into the Redwood tokenizer metadata. e.g.:
```
for k, t in tokenizer.special_tokens_map.items():
    special_ids[k] = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(t)
# then write special_ids into redwood_tokenizer.json
```
michael: good. Also add a sanity check step that asserts tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(special_ids[k]) == t for every mapping.
jordan: long-term: when we quantize/compile the model we must avoid any code path that reassigns ids. Bake the mapping into the model config and KV cache handling. Add unit tests that load HF artifacts -> convert -> run sample prompts and compare logprobs for a handful of reference tokens.
anya: I can make a PR to the conversion script. Quick patch I tested locally:
```
# where we used to just append tokens
added = tokenizer.added_tokens
for tok in added:
    assigned_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tok)
    redwood_meta['added_tokens_map'][tok] = str(assigned_id)
```
That preserved the original id values in the redwood artifact and fixed the safety regression in my local smoke run.
infra-bot: deploy plan: canary conversion of 3 models with mapped special token ids, run eval-bot pipeline, promote if pass.
michael: also document edge-cases: some HF tokenizers return -1 for unknown tokens (they expect adding converts them). If convert_tokens_to_ids returns -1, don't trust it — instead call tokenizer.add_tokens first and then re-query (or fail conversion and flag for manual review).
anya: added a lint step too: if any of eos/bos/pad/unk ids differ from baseline mapping file, mark thread as WARNING and prevent auto-promote.
jordan: good. also add a small script for debugging mapping drift:
```
# debug script
for t in ['','<|pad|>','<|unk|>','<|sep|>']:
    print(t, hf_tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(t), redwood_meta.get('added_tokens_map', {}).get(t))
```
samir: one more gotcha — chat templates that embed literal token strings (eg. system message includes '' token) can break if template authors relied on a specific id. Avoid literal-id checks; always compare tokens by string or use tokenizer functions.
anya: thanks all, will open PR and include the eval results + a regression unit test. tagging @michael for review. :thumbsup:
michael: ack, I'll review today. let's also add a CI gate so future HF->Redwood conversions fail fast if special token ids drift.
anya: thanks — leaving action items in the PR.
